category_scheme.method: Editorial primary-genre or primary-subject classification. Each library title is counted once; a box set remains one library title. Categories may overlap conceptually, but counts do not.

categories.name: Science fiction
categories.definition: Space opera, military science fiction, speculative technology, and science-fiction thrillers.

categories.name: Thrillers, espionage & mystery
categories.definition: Crime, espionage, military suspense, contemporary techno-thrillers, and supernatural suspense.

categories.name: Fantasy
categories.definition: Epic and urban fantasy, including the Convergence series.

categories.name: Literary classics & mythology
categories.definition: Classic literary fiction, historical adventure, and ancient epic poetry.

categories.name: History, military & politics
categories.definition: Historical accounts, military history, political investigations, and nuclear-risk analysis.

categories.name: Business, leadership & productivity
categories.definition: Management, entrepreneurship, negotiation, career development, and work organization.

categories.name: Biography, memoir & personal essays
categories.definition: Life stories and autobiographical essays, including the David Sedaris collections.

categories.name: Society & culture
categories.definition: Social criticism, cultural commentary, and architecture criticism.

categories.name: Educational — science, data & learning
categories.definition: Education theory, statistics, data-driven reasoning, and behavioral science; excludes history and practical business/self-help books counted elsewhere.

categories.name: Parenting & relationships
categories.definition: Parenting, child development, and marriage guidance.

categories.name: Personal development & psychology
categories.definition: Personal habits, emotional growth, and vulnerability.

boundary_notes: Science fiction includes Red Rising, the Void Trilogy, and the Infinite Timeline despite fantasy or thriller elements. Four Minutes and Quantum Radio are counted here for their speculative premises.
Convergence is urban fantasy and is counted with fantasy, alongside Lightbringer and The Age of Madness.
Beneath the Dark Ice is counted as supernatural suspense; Kill Decision is counted as a techno-thriller.
The Iliad and The Three Musketeers are literary classics, not nonfiction history.

History includes The Making of the Atomic Bomb (cataloged as Making of the Atomic Bomb), Titan II, and Nuclear War: A Scenario; the last is forward-looking risk analysis rather than a historical narrative.
Educational is a narrow category: Norms and Nobility, The Consuming Instinct, How to Lie with Statistics, and Super Crunchers. It is not an umbrella total for all nonfiction.
